mainTopic: Which תנא holds that one איסור can take effect on another (רבי מאיר or רבי שמעון), טעה בדבר מצוה, and why the women in the משנה are separated.
overview: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that a new איסור can take effect on top of an old one in all three ways: איסור כולל, איסור מוסיף, and איסור בת אחת. רב says it is רבי מאיר, and proves it from a ברייתא about one bite that brings four חטאות and one אשם, with רבי מאיר adding שבת. The גמרא then asks whose view רבי מאיר follows on someone who sinned by mistake while doing a מצוה. One answer is רבי אליעזר. The other is that רבי יהושע exempts only a person who was rushed for time, as with מילה or תרומה on ערב פסח. A second answer to the opening question says the משנה can follow רבי שמעון if all the איסורים began at the same moment. רב explains that even נדה can start at that moment, if the women were bleeding through the birthdays when the men and women became adults. Next the גמרא asks why the women are separated, if a woman cannot conceive from her first act, and answers that the couples had relations twice. It then explains that רבי חייא's sixteen חטאות count only the first act. The amud ends as רבא begins a challenge to רב נחמן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who holds that all three kinds of piled-up prohibitions take effect?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that an איסור כולל, an איסור מוסיף, and an איסור בת אחת can all take effect on top of an existing איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is this תנא who holds that an איסור כולל, an איסור מוסיף, and an איסור בת אחת all take effect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view that the earlier case depends on. That view is that new איסורים can land on top of old ones in all three ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is a rule that אין איסור חל על איסור, meaning a second איסור cannot take effect where one already exists. The exceptions are a broader איסור, an added איסור, or one that comes at the same moment. The earlier case needs all three exceptions to work, so the גמרא wants to know whose opinion that is.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period
A broader איסור that also covers new people or things that were not forbidden before
An איסור that adds a new kind of restriction to the same person or thing
Two איסורים that take effect at the exact same moment

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether these איסורים exist. Everyone agrees they exist. The question is whether the second איסור actually takes effect, so that a person is liable for it too, when an איסור was already there.

phrases.english: And who is this תנא
phrases.notes: He means the תנא behind the earlier case, where רבי חייא counted sixteen חטאות.

phrases.english: who holds of a broader prohibition
and an added prohibition
and a simultaneous prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about whose view the earlier case follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that איסור כולל, איסור מוסיף, and איסור בת אחת all take effect on top of an existing איסור.

steps.title: The answer: it is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says that this view belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the תנא is רבי מאיר. The next step brings the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step only names the opinion. The proof comes right after, from a ברייתא that shows רבי מאיר counting many איסורים for one act.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view that all three kinds of איסור take effect belongs to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: One bite, four sin-offerings and one guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one act of eating can make a person liable for four חטאות and one אשם. This happens when a טמא person eats חלב that is נותר from קדשים on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: There is a person who eats one eating and is liable for four חטאות and one אשם. This is a טמא person who ate חלב that was נותר from קדשים, on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves רב's claim. It shows one act of eating that breaks many איסורים at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four חטאות are for eating קודש while טמא, eating חלב, eating נותר, and eating on יום הכפורים. The אשם is for מעילה, using הקדש for oneself. Each of these איסורים came on top of the earlier חלב איסור, in a broader or an added way. So this ברייתא holds that such איסורים do take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering, brought for doing an איסור by mistake
A guilt-offering, here for מעילה (misusing הקדש)
Forbidden fat of an animal
Meat of a קרבן left past its time to be eaten
Consecrated items, קדשים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear case where one act counts as many separate sins. That only works if every איסור beyond the first one actually took effect.

phrases.english: As it is taught: There is one who eats a single eating
and is liable for it four sin-offerings
and one guilt-offering.
An impure person who ate forbidden fat,
and it was leftover from consecrated offerings,
phrases.notes: So the fat is also הקדש. That is where the אשם for מעילה comes from.

phrases.english: on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports רב's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds that איסור כולל and איסור מוסיף take effect on top of an existing איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing four חטאות and one אשם for one act of eating.

steps.title: רבי מאיר adds carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that if it was שבת and the person carried the food out in his mouth, he is liable for that as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: If it was שבת and he carried it out in his mouth, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר adds one more חטאת: carrying the food from one domain to another on שבת, inside his mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום הכפורים falls on שבת, both איסורים begin at the same moment. That makes them an איסור בת אחת. Since רבי מאיר counts the שבת liability too, he holds that even a simultaneous איסור takes effect. This completes the proof that he holds all three kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: He carried it out from one domain to another, a מלאכה on שבת
In his mouth

steps.whatToRemember: The first part of the ברייתא shows איסור כולל and איסור מוסיף. רבי מאיר's addition about שבת shows איסור בת אחת. Together they prove that רבי מאיר holds all three.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
If it was Shabbat
phrases.notes: He means יום הכפורים fell on שבת, so both days began at the same moment.

phrases.english: and he carried it out in his mouth, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר אִם הָיְתָה שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, adding רבי מאיר's extra liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If it was שבת and he carried the food out in his mouth, he owes another חטאת for carrying on שבת.

steps.title: The חכמים: carrying is a different kind of sin
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי מאיר that the שבת liability does not belong in the list, because it is not about eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It is not of the same type.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי מאיר's addition. Carrying is a different kind of sin than eating, so it should not be counted in a list about one act of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their objection is about what belongs in the list. The ברייתא counts liabilities that come from eating, and carrying comes from a different act. They do not argue about the איסור בת אחת idea itself, so רבי מאיר's view on that point still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not of the same type, meaning not from the same kind of act

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים are saying the person is free from the שבת חטאת. They only say it does not belong in a list of liabilities from eating.

phrases.english: They said to him:
It is not of the same type.
phrases.notes: Literally 'not from the name.' He means carrying is not an act of eating, so it is not part of this list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים respond to רבי מאיר's addition inside the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only counting the שבת liability within the list of liabilities from one act of eating.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Carrying is a different act from eating, so it is not the same type of liability.

steps.title: Whose view on erring in a מצוה does רבי מאיר follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier תנא רבי מאיר follows. It cannot be רבי יהושע, who exempts a person who made a mistake while doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, whose view does he follow? If he follows רבי יהושע, there is a problem. רבי יהושע said that someone who made a mistake while doing a מצוה is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which side of an older מחלוקת רבי מאיר is following. It rules out רבי יהושע right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה the brothers sinned by mistake while trying to do a מצוה. רבי יהושע holds that a mistake made in the middle of doing a מצוה brings no חטאת. Since רבי מאיר does make them liable, he cannot be following רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Made a mistake while trying to do a מצוה
Exempt (here, from bringing a חטאת)
But didn't he say?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir, according to whose view does he hold?
If according to Rabbi Yehoshua, but he said:
One who erred in a matter of a מצוה is exempt.
phrases.notes: He means someone who sinned by accident while he was busy trying to do a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question about the רבי מאיר view identified in steps 2-4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר or רבי יהושע on טָעָה בִּדְבַר מִצְוָה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהושע is ruled out, רבי מאיר must follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a person who sins by mistake is חייב a חטאת even if he was trying to do a מצוה. That fits רבי מאיר making the brothers liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it must be
Liable
Sin-offering brought for an accidental sin

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by elimination.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר, who makes a person liable even when he erred while doing a מצוה.

steps.title: Even רבי יהושע could agree, because his exemption is only for someone who is rushed
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: רבי מאיר can follow רבי יהושע after all. רבי יהושע only exempts in the case of the babies, where the person is rushed. The brothers were not rushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this: really he follows רבי יהושע. When רבי יהושע said that one who erred in a מצוה is פטור, he meant the case of the babies, where the person is rushed for time. But here, since the person is not rushed, he is not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer, so רבי מאיר does not have to follow רבי אליעזר. It limits רבי יהושע's rule to cases where the person was under time pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a ברית מילה the day is fixed, so the מוהל hurries, and that rush can cause the mistake. רבי יהושע exempts only that kind of mistake. Marriage has no deadline, so even רבי יהושע would make the brothers liable.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say this (introduces another answer)
Really, in truth
These words apply only to
Babies (the case of babies mixed up for מילה)
His time is rushed, he is under time pressure

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a new way to read רבי יהושע. His exemption depends on the person being rushed, not just on his doing a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: If you wish, say: actually it is according to Rabbi Yehoshua.
When Rabbi Yehoshua said
one who erred in a matter of a מצוה is exempt,
this applies to the case of babies,
phrases.notes: This is the case where babies got mixed up and the מוהל did a ברית on שבת for the wrong baby.

phrases.english: since his time is pressed;
but this case,
since his time is not pressed, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to step 7 by narrowing רבי יהושע's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע exempts anyone who erred while doing a מצוה, so רבי מאיר cannot follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע exempts only when the person was rushed for time, so in the unrushed marriage case he agrees there is liability.

steps.title: Challenge from תרומה, where nobody is rushed and רבי יהושע still exempts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'rushed' idea. In the case of a כהן who ate תרומה and turned out to be disqualified, there is no time pressure, yet רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at תרומה. There the person is not rushed, and רבי יהושע still exempts. As we learned in a משנה: A man was eating תרומה, and it became known that he is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a חלוצה. רבי אליעזר makes him pay the principal plus a fifth, and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 8 with a משנה about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן גרושה or בן חלוצה is not a real כהן, so he may not eat תרומה. He thought he was doing a מצוה by eating it. Eating תרומה has no deadline, yet רבי יהושע exempts him, which suggests that being rushed is not the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at (opens a challenge)
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only כהנים may eat
Son of a divorcée and a כהן, who is not fit to be a כהן
Son of a woman who did חליצה and a כהן, who is also not fit to be a כהן
The principal value plus an extra fifth, paid by a non-כהן who ate תרומה by mistake

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי תְּרוּמָה, דְּאֵין זְמַנּוֹ בָּהוּל, וְקָפָטַר!
phrases.english: But there is teruma, where his time is not pressed, and yet he exempts!
As we learned: If he was eating teruma

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.english: and it became known that he is the son of a divorcée or the son of a ḥalutza,
Rabbi Eliezer obligates him in the principal and the fifth,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי תְּרוּמָה, דְּאֵין זְמַנּוֹ בָּהוּל, וְקָפָטַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהושע exempts only when the person is rushed for time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the תרומה case there seems to be no time pressure, yet רבי יהושע still exempts, so 'rushed' cannot be the condition.

steps.title: The תרומה case is on ערב פסח, when he really is rushed
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי already explained that the תרומה משנה is about ערב פסח. The person was rushing to eat the חמץ תרומה before the time ran out, so that case fits the 'rushed' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already said about that משנה: רב ביבי בר אביי said, here we are dealing with תרומה on ערב פסח, when the time is rushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting an earlier explanation of the תרומה משנה. That explanation shows the person there really was under time pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח, חמץ of תרומה must be eaten before the deadline or it has to be burned, so the כהן hurries. That means the תרומה case is also a 'rushed' case. The answer of step 8 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was already stated about it
Here we are dealing with
The day before פסח, when חמץ must be finished by a set time

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain רבי מאיר. Either he follows רבי אליעזר, or he follows רבי יהושע, whose exemption applies only when a person is rushed, as with מילה or תרומה on ערב פסח. The brothers in our משנה were not rushed, so they are liable either way.
steps.confusionAlert: The תרומה here is a case of חמץ. The time pressure comes from פסח, not from anything about תרומה itself.

phrases.english: But it was stated about it:
Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
Here we are dealing with teruma on the eve of Passover,
phrases.notes: The תרומה is חמץ. It has to be eaten before the deadline, or else it must be burned.

phrases.english: whose time is pressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and saves the distinction of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תרומה case has no time pressure, so it disproves the 'rushed' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תרומה case is on ערב פסח, when the כהן is rushed, so it fits the 'rushed' rule.

steps.title: The משנה can also follow רבי שמעון through simultaneous prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: the משנה is not following רבי מאיר. It follows רבי שמעון, in a case where all the prohibitions started at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say the משנה is talking about prohibitions that all start at once, and it follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to explain why the brothers are liable for several prohibitions at once. It says the משנה can follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון normally holds that a second prohibition cannot take hold on top of one that already exists. He agrees, though, that if several prohibitions start at the exact same moment, they all take effect together. So the משנה works for him if every prohibition began at the same instant.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another answer
Prohibitions that start at one and the same moment
According to the view of

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי שמעון generally lets one prohibition land on another. He only allows it when they all start at the same instant.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
it is a case of prohibitions that come at one time,
and it follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 1, as an alternative to רב's answer in step 2 that it is רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the משנה to a different תנא by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The multiple liabilities only work according to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: They also work for רבי שמעון if all the prohibitions began at the same moment.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can follow רבי שמעון if all its prohibitions are איסור בת אחת, taking effect at the same moment.

steps.title: How could the נדה prohibition start at the same moment?
steps.stepSummary: The other prohibitions can all start together through agents who meet. But how can נדה start at that same moment?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that all the other prohibitions can start together: the men appointed an agent, the women appointed an agent, and the two agents met. But how can you find נדה starting at that same time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new explanation. It accepts that the marriage prohibitions can start at once, but asks how נדה can start at that very moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one agent marries off both brothers and one agent accepts for both sisters, all four marriages happen at once. That makes אשת אח and אחות אשה start together. Being a נדה, however, depends on the women's bodies and not on the marriages, so it is hard to see how it could begin at that same instant.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense with respect to; sets up a contrast with a difficulty
Agent
The status of a נדה, a menstruating woman
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: It makes sense that you can find all the others:
where they (the men) appointed an agent,
and they (the women) appointed an agent,
and one agent met the other agent.
phrases.notes: When the two agents meet, all the marriages happen in the same instant.

phrases.english: But נדה, how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the simultaneous-prohibition model from step 11 can include נדה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 11 that all the משנה's prohibitions began at once
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marriage prohibitions can be timed together through agents, but נדה status is not created by the marriage, so it seems it cannot start at the same moment.

steps.title: רב times the נדה status to the moment of adulthood
steps.stepSummary: The women were bleeding without stopping from before the men's 13th birthday until after it, and from before the women's 12th birthday until after it. Liability for everything therefore starts at one moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said in the name of רב: The case is where the women kept bleeding from inside the 13th year until after 13, to make the men liable, and from inside the 12th year until after 12, to make the women liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that נדה can start at the same moment as the other prohibitions. Liability begins at adulthood, and the women were already bleeding when that moment came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy becomes liable at 13 and a girl at 12. If the brothers turned 13 and the sisters turned 12 on the same day, and the women were bleeding straight through that day, then every prohibition, נדה included, starts to count against them at the same instant. That fits רבי שמעון's rule of simultaneous prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: Bleeding continuously, without a break
From within ... until after
To make liable

phrases.english: Rav Amram said in the name of Rav:
where they were bleeding continuously from within thirteen
until after thirteen —
to make them (the men) liable,

phrases.aramaic: מִתּוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר —
phrases.english: from within twelve until after twelve —
to make them (the women) liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12 by building a precise timing case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific scenario
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נדה status could not possibly start at the same moment as the marriage prohibitions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since liability begins at adulthood, continuous bleeding across that birthday makes נדה start together with everything else.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the משנה works only if every prohibition began at once: the marriages through two agents who met, and נדה through continuous bleeding across the birthdays of adulthood.

steps.title: Why separate them if a woman cannot conceive from her first time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the women are separated for three months, then asks why, since a woman does not become pregnant from her first act.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'We separate them.' But a woman does not become pregnant from the first act!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and quotes it. It then challenges it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The women are separated for three months to check whether they are pregnant from the wrong man. The גמרא assumes a woman cannot conceive from her very first act. If so, there seems to be nothing to check.

keyTerms.meaning: We separate them (from their husbands)
Becomes pregnant
First act of relations

phrases.english: "We separate them."
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה: the women are kept apart for three months.

phrases.english: But a woman does not become pregnant
from the first act of relations!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְרִישִׁים אוֹתָן. וְהָא אֵין אִשָּׁה מִתְעַבֶּרֶת בְּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of whose view the משנה follows and opens a new discussion about the three-month separation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the women are separated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separation is only needed if pregnancy is possible, and a woman cannot conceive from her first act.

steps.title: They had relations twice
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, answers that the couples had relations a second time, so pregnancy is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: It is a case where they had relations and then did so again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The couples had relations more than once, so the women could have conceived the second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a woman cannot conceive only applies to the first act. Once there was a second act, pregnancy is a real possibility. That makes the three months of separation necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: They had relations and then repeated it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Where they had relations and did it again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14 by changing the facts of the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific scenario
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one act, so pregnancy was impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were two acts, so pregnancy is possible and separation is needed.

steps.title: רבי חייא counted only sixteen חטאות
steps.stepSummary: If there were two acts, why did רבי חייא count sixteen חטאות? With two acts there should be thirty-two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about רבי חייא's teaching: 'Here there are sixteen חטאות'? It should be thirty-two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15. It uses a ברייתא of רבי חייא that counts the sin-offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא counted sixteen חטאות for the four people. If each couple sinned twice, every prohibition was broken twice, which doubles the total to thirty-two. So רבי חייא's count seems to show there was only one act.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offerings, brought for sins done by mistake
Thirty-two

phrases.english: But then, that which Rabbi Chiya taught:
"Here there are sixteen sin-offerings,"
it should be thirty-two!
phrases.notes: Two acts means every sin happened twice, so sixteen becomes thirty-two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15 with רבי חייא's count.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's answer that they had relations twice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two acts would double the sin-offerings to thirty-two, but רבי חייא counts only sixteen.

steps.title: רבי חייא was only counting the first act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא's count of sixteen covers only the first act of relations. It proves this from רבי אליעזר's view, where the number would otherwise be huge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, according to רבי אליעזר, who makes a person liable for every single movement, the count would be very large. So you must say רבי חייא is counting only the first movement. In the same way, he is counting only the first act of relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why רבי חייא said sixteen and not thirty-two. He was only counting the חטאות from the first act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא turns the question back: if every act had to be counted, then according to רבי אליעזר, who gives a separate חטאת for every movement, the number would be enormous. Since רבי חייא obviously did not count every movement, his number must refer only to the beginning. So his sixteen refers only to the first ביאה, and the second ביאה is simply not included in his count.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning: a way of turning the question back on the one who asked it
A single movement within one act of relations
A lot, many
He is counting
The first act of relations

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא's number, sixteen, is a count of the first act only. It does not mean the couples had relations only once.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the second act carries no חטאת. It is only saying that רבי חייא chose to count just the first act.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects רב נחמן's earlier answer, that there were two acts, from the challenge raised in step 16.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, according to Rabbi Eliezer,
who holds one liable for each and every thrusting movement,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר's view: each movement counts as its own sin, needing its own חטאת.

phrases.english: there would be many.
Rather, he is counting the first movement only;
so too, he is counting the first act of intercourse only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by showing that רבי חייא's count was never meant to include every act.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the scope of the count, backed by a parallel from רבי אליעזר's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא's sixteen should include every act of relations, so two acts should mean thirty-two.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא counts only the first act, just as according to רבי אליעזר he would count only the first movement.

steps.title: רבא turns to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: An opening line: רבא begins speaking to רב נחמן, setting up a new challenge to his answer about the second act.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. The גמרא is introducing רבא, who is about to challenge רב נחמן. The challenge itself comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן had answered, in step 15, that the women must be separated because there was a second act, since a woman does not become pregnant from the first. רבא is now about to question that answer. The actual words of his challenge come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, a leading אמורא, here challenging his teacher

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the count question is settled, the גמרא sets up a new challenge to רב נחמן's answer from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's answer in step 15 that the couples had relations a second time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the opening attribution appears here. The content of the challenge follows on the next amud.
